newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: CAIRN'S BANGLADESH GASFIELD SEEN STARTING NEXT MAY.
newsitem.headline: CAIRN'S BANGLADESH GASFIELD SEEN STARTING NEXT MAY.

text.p: Britain's Cairn Energy Plc should begin commercial extraction of natural gas off the shores of Bangladesh by next May, a state energy official said on Wednesday.
The company triggered global interest in the South Asian country's hydrocarbon potential when it found the gas field last year.

"Cairn is going ahead with a target to produce 160 million cubic feet (MCF) of gas per day from the Shangu field from April 30," a senior official of the state- owned oil and gas agency, Petrobangla, told Reuters on Wednesday.
Construction of a 53 km (30 mile) pipeline is expected to start from November.
"The offshore platform is now being fabricated in Singapore which will be shipped to the field by early April," said the official.
Brown & Root, a subsidiary of the U.S. Halliburton company is responsible for the pipeline and platform construction under a deal with Cairn.
"It will be a big occasion. The production will greatly help fill the shortfall of gas in our power stations and factories," said another Petrobangla official.
The company has already signed a gas purchase agreement with the Bangladesh government.
Cairn has already drilled three wells in the Shangu field off the Chittagong coast which Petrobangla officials said has an estimated reserves of 850 billion cubic feet of gas.
Three more wells were expected to be drilled before commercial production begins, they said.
Cairn has recently struck a deal with a Royal Dutch/Shell subsidiary to jointly developing the Shangu field in block no 16.
Cairn and its partners were expected to invest around $250 million for the development of the Shangu field, Petrobangla officials said.

The British company, which has production sharing contract (PSC) with Petrobangla for two of the Bangladesh's total 23 hydrocrbon blocks, recently began drilling in block number 15 in the southeastern hill tracts area.
Cairn, jointly with Shell, has sought exploration rights for another six blocks in the latest bidding round closed on July 15.

Some 20 multinational oil and gas companies and a state-run Bangladesh company participated in the bidding for exploration rights to explore 12 remaining blocks in Bangladesh, nine onshore and three offshore.
The proposals are being evaluated by foreign consultants and the Energy Ministry officials said exploration deals with the successful bidders would be signed by December this year.
Bangladesh has proven gas reserves of 10.2 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of natural gas
But the Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan told reporters last month the country's potential gas reserves were between 50 TCF and 80 TCF.
